PROPOSED CENTRAL INTUITION (for approval):
  "ADLB is one row per subject, per parameter, per timepoint: PARAM says
   what was measured, AVAL says what it was, and ABLFL nominates the one
   row the analysis calls baseline — so that every change in the trial
   is measured from a point the SAP chose, not one the lab happened to
   flag."

========================================================================
VERIFY LIST — every ADaM specific this session intends to assert.

--- Structure ---

L1 [ADaMIG v1.3 §2.3.2] BDS contains "1 or more records per subject, per
   analysis parameter, per analysis timepoint." Analysis timepoint is
   CONDITIONALLY required depending on the analysis; with no timepoint
   the structure is one or more records per subject per parameter.
   Also §2.3.2: BDS datasets "do not have counterparts in SDTM" — the
   resemblance to the Findings class is superficial, since BDS may be
   derived from Findings, Events, Interventions, Special-purpose
   domains, other ADaM datasets, or any combination.

L2 [ADaMIG v1.3 §2.3.2] "Although the ADSL is a source for
   subject-level variables used in BDS datasets, this does not mean that
   every ADSL variable should be included in the BDS dataset." Carry
   what the analysis needs, not everything.

--- Parameters ---

L3 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.4.1, Table 3.3.4.1.1] PARAM (Req) "must include all
   descriptive and qualifying information relevant to the analysis
   purpose of the parameter" and "should be sufficient to describe
   unambiguously the contents of AVAL and/or AVALC". Units are named as
   a candidate qualifier. Max 200 chars (40 if it will become a variable
   label in a transposed dataset). "In contrast to SDTM --TEST, no
   additional variable is needed to further qualify PARAM." PARAM must
   be present and populated on EVERY record.

L4 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.4.1] PARAMCD (Req): <=8 characters, must START WITH
   A LETTER (not underscore), comprised only of A-Z, underscore and 0-9
   — so that a transposed dataset yields valid variable names. One-to-one
   with PARAM within a dataset. Populated on every record. PARAMN (Perm)
   one-to-one with PARAM; if populated on any record for a PARAM it must
   be populated on every record for that PARAM. PARCATy (Perm) is a
   categorisation, many-to-one, NOT a qualifier for PARAM.
   (Re-cited from adam-concepts, which previewed these constraints.)

L5 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.4.1] AVAL (Num, Cond) and AVALC (Char, Cond):
   "either AVAL or AVALC must be present in the dataset"; AVAL is
   required if AVALC is not present and vice versa. On a given record it
   is permissible for either or both to be null. If both are populated
   within a parameter there must be a one-to-one relationship between
   them; AVALC "should not be used to categorize the values of AVAL"
   (AVALCATy is for that).

--- Baseline: the thread's payoff ---

L6 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.8, Table 3.3.8.1] ABLFL (Char, value "Y", Cond)
   identifies "the baseline record for each subject, parameter, and
   baseline type (BASETYPE) combination". Conditionality is exact:
   "ABLFL is required if BASE is present in the dataset." Also: "a
   baseline record may be derived (e.g., it may be an average), in which
   case DTYPE must also be populated." ABLFN (Perm) is its numeric
   counterpart, one-to-one, both-or-neither populated.

L7 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.4.1] BASE (Num, Cond) "contains the value of AVAL
   copied from a record within the parameter on which ABLFL = 'Y'".
   Required if the dataset supports analysis or review of numeric
   baseline value or functions of it. And the integrity rule: "if BASE
   is populated for a parameter, and BASE is non-null for a subject for
   that parameter, then there must be a record flagged by ABLFL for that
   subject and parameter."

L8 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.4.1] CHG (Perm) "Equal to AVAL-BASE"; PCHG (Perm)
   "Equal to ((AVAL-BASE)/BASE)*100". Both "should be populated for all
   post-baseline records of that PARAM regardless of whether that record
   is used for analysis", and — a precision worth teaching — "the
   decision on how to populate pre-baseline and baseline values of CHG
   is left to producer choice." So CHG at baseline being 0 vs null is a
   documented sponsor decision, not a rule.
   AUTHOR DECISION NEEDED (see decision 2 below).

L9 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.4.1] BASETYPE (Char, Cond) is "producer-defined
   text describing the definition of baseline relevant to the value of
   BASE on the current record", "required when there are multiple ways
   that baseline is defined", and if used for any PARAM must be non-null
   for ALL records of that PARAM where BASE or BASEC is non-null.
   GLPX-001 has ONE baseline definition, so BASETYPE is not required and
   is not built — taught as concept, with the pointer to §4.2.1.6 Rule 6
   for the multiple-baseline case.

L10 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.5, Table 3.3.5.1] DTYPE (Char, codelist DTYPE,
    extensible, Cond) "is used to denote, and must be populated, when
    the value of AVAL or AVALC has been imputed or derived differently
    than the other analysis values within the parameter", and is
    "required to be populated even if AVAL and AVALC are null on the
    derived record". For each DTYPE value "the precise derivation
    algorithm must be defined in analysis variable metadata, even for
    DTYPE values in the CDISC Controlled Terminology."
    GLPX-001: every AVAL is an observed lab result and the baseline is
    an observed record, so DTYPE is NULL throughout — which is itself
    the lesson (null DTYPE = "this row is what was measured").

--- Timing ---

L11 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.3, Table 3.3.3.1] ADT (Cond) "the date associated
    with AVAL and/or AVALC"; ADY (Cond) "the relative day of AVAL and/or
    AVALC. The number of days from an anchor date (NOT NECESSARILY
    DM.RFSTDTC) to ADT." — the SAME parenthesis as OCCDS's ASTDY, so the
    ADAE lesson transfers exactly. Also: "if a dataset contains more than
    one record per parameter per subject, then an SDTM or ADaM relative
    timing variable must be present (ADY would meet this requirement)"
    — which for ADLB makes ADY effectively mandatory. ADTF (Cond,
    DATEFL) required if ADT was imputed.

L12 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.3, Table 3.3.3.1] AVISIT (Char, Cond) "required if
    an analysis is done by nominal, assigned or analysis visit". Key
    precisions: "AVISIT is a derived field and does not have to map to
    VISIT from the SDTM"; "AVISIT represents the analysis visit of the
    record, but it does not mean that the record was analyzed"; "values
    of AVISIT are producer-defined"; and its derivation "should be
    indicated in the variable metadata". AVISITN (Perm) numeric
    counterpart.

--- Ranges ---

L13 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.7, Table 3.3.7.1] ANRLO/ANRHI (analysis normal
    range lower/upper), ANRIND (Analysis Reference Range Indicator), and
    BNRIND ("ANRIND of the baseline record identified by ABLFL").
    These are the ADaM analysis versions of SDTM's LBORNRLO/LBORNRHI and
    LBNRIND — same re-derivation principle as the flags.
    VERIFY AT PROSE TIME: confirm each Core designation from the table
    (read as Perm) before citing; I have not yet read the Core column
    for every row of 3.3.7.1.

--- Identifiers, treatment, traceability ---

L14 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.1, Table 3.3.1.1] STUDYID, USUBJID Req; SUBJID,
    SITEID Perm ("required in ADSL, but permissible in other datasets"
    — the mirror of the ADSL claim S2). ASEQ (Perm) "sequence number
    given to ensure uniqueness of subject records within an ADaM
    dataset", useful "when the dataset is used as input to another ADaM
    dataset".

L15 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.2, Table 3.3.2.1] TRTP (Cond) / TRTA are
    record-level treatment variables; "at least one treatment variable
    is required even in non-randomized trials", satisfied by any
    subject- or record-level treatment variable (TRTxxP, TRTP, TRTA).
    If populated, TRTP "must match at least one value of the character
    planned treatment variables in ADSL". GLPX is single-period, so
    TRTP = ADSL.TRT01P and TRTA = ADSL.TRT01A on every row.

L16 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.9, Table 3.3.9.1] SRCDOM / SRCVAR / SRCSEQ (all
    Perm) give datapoint traceability: source domain, source variable,
    source sequence number. Note the contrast with ADAE — OCCDS
    explicitly EXCLUDES SRCVAR because it names the variable deriving
    AVAL/AVALC and OCCDS has no AVAL (OCCDS v1.1, §3.2.2). Here AVAL
    exists, so SRCVAR is meaningful: SRCDOM="LB", SRCVAR="LBSTRESN",
    SRCSEQ=LBSEQ.

L17 [ADaMIG v1.3 §3.3.8] ANLzzFL (Cond) is "to be used in addition to
    other selection variables when the other selection variables in
    combination are insufficient to identify the exact set of records
    used for one or more analyses". GLPX-001 has exactly one row per
    subject per parameter per visit (verified: TRUE), so USUBJID +
    PARAMCD + AVISIT already identify records uniquely and ANL01FL is
    NOT required. Taught as concept + why it is absent here.

C1 DTYPE codelist — confirm it exists in sdtm.terminology and is

C2 NRIND codelist for ANRIND values (NORMAL/HIGH/LOW), same codelist

All pasted as real output; none recalled.

--- Explicitly NOT asserted / deferred ---
- Time-to-event variables (§3.3.6) — named, not built.
- Criteria variables CRITy/CRITyFL (§3.3.4.3) — out of scope.
- Analysis visit WINDOWING (§3.3.5, Table 3.3.5.2) — GLPX visits are
  already clean nominal visits; windowing named, not built.
- VS (vital signs) — this session is labs only.
========================================================================

GLPX LB DATA REALITY (probed, for sizing):
  12388 rows, 400 subjects, 4 tests (ALT/CREAT/GLUC/HBA1C), 8 visits
  (SCREENING, BASELINE, WEEK 4/8/12/16/20/26). 3097 rows per test.
  One row per subject/test/visit — VERIFIED unique, no duplicates
  (D6 was removed during the SDTM build).
  No null LBSTRESN. D7 (blank unit) was resolved in SDTM: units are
  populated for 101-037.
  LBNRIND: HIGH 6520 / NORMAL 5774 / LOW 94.
  D5 lives at SCREENING: 101-052, HbA1c 13.9%, HIGH (range 4.0-5.6).

  *** THE BASELINE PAYOFF, QUANTIFIED ***
  1600 subject-test pairs. SDTM LBLOBXFL lands on SCREENING for 1300
  of them (81.2%) and on BASELINE for 300. So an ABLFL defined as "the
  BASELINE visit record" DISAGREES with LBLOBXFL on 1300 pairs.
  Every one of the 400 subjects has at least one test that disagrees
  (165 disagree on all four; 235 on some).
  Screening and baseline values coincide for only 86 of 1600 pairs, so
  the disagreement is almost always a different NUMBER, not just a
  different row.
  Impact on the headline result (HbA1c, week 26 mean change):
    ABLFL baseline  : GLPX -1.363, Placebo -0.294, difference -1.069
    LBLOBXFL instead: GLPX -1.440, Placebo -0.306, difference -1.138
  A 0.069 %-point shift in the primary endpoint from choosing the wrong
  baseline flag. Small, real, and not the number the SAP defined —
  frame it exactly that way, do NOT overclaim it as decisive.

INFRASTRUCTURE: build_adam.R gains build_adlb() -> committed
data/adam/adlb.csv, completing data/adam/ for the TLF sessions.

## When Do You Use This? {#sec-adlb}

TODO (prose pass): scenarios — the primary endpoint is a *change* from
baseline, so something must define baseline; a safety review needs every
lab value classified against its reference range at every visit; a
reviewer needs to see the measured value and the analysis value side by
side. Ends with the bold question: **when the whole trial is measured as
change from baseline, who decides which value baseline is?** Builds on
[ADaM Concepts](adam-concepts.qmd), [ADSL](adsl.qmd), and
[Findings](sdtm-findings.qmd) where `LBLOBXFL` was deliberately left
unfinished.
